steps.what: Hear the commercial brief for advertising jingles or film soundtracks
Choose the musical hook, length and mood
Write the music into the notation score
Play the jingle or soundtrack for the commissioners

tasks.design: Nothing is generated. She hears the commercial brief, writes the jingle or soundtrack at the piano into the notation file in {OTHER}, and plays it for the people who asked. The machine does not appear.
tasks.previous_blocker: The musical idea is the work. A template cannot hear whether a jingle fits the brief.
tasks.enabler_now: No enabler changes this task. The notation file already holds the score she writes.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the hook and judging the playback stay with her ear.
tasks.human_edge: She decides the music and hears whether the commissioners accept the feel of it.
tasks.altitude: Nothing in the week changes. She still writes commercial music and plays it back.

reach.task: Time a soundtrack cue to a picture
reach.learn: The length and the hit points the picture allows

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: writing a jingle or a film soundtrack is composition. The digest says composing stays with the person. No product in the digest writes the musical idea.

assumptions: The focal role is the composer. She writes the commercial music today. No machine step is added.
The brief is heard in the room. This task does not send the score outside the organisation.
No tool is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a producer must accept the cue before it later leaves the company. That acceptance is not part of this task.
research_questions: How often the brief arrives as a timed picture rather than a spoken mood.

already_counted.description: Hearing the brief, choosing the hook, writing the score and playing it back all stay.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Writing and playback stay with her, so no hour moves.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the source music for that voice or instrument
Name the instrument that will accommodate those musicians
Transpose the music onto the named instrument
Play the transposed music and fix unreachable notes
Place the corrected part in the ensemble score

tasks.design: She names the target instrument. The notation file in {OTHER} then shifts every pitched note by that interval into a draft part. She plays the draft with the musician and places the corrected part in {DOCS} herself. The shift does not choose the instrument and does not file the part.
tasks.previous_blocker: She recopied every note by hand. The interval was fixed, but the copy was still her hour.
tasks.enabler_now: A notation file that already stores pitch and duration can shift those notes by a named interval. That is configuration, not a new composition tool.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the line sits in that musician's range, and whether a missing pitch can be guessed, stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the instrument and hears the part before anyone else uses it.

ambition.what: Transposed parts the same week for instruments she rarely writes out

tasks.altitude: Recopying onto another instrument takes less of the hour when the source already has pitches. She still names the instrument, still plays the part, and still places the corrected part herself.

reach.task: Set a vocal line singers in the scene can reach
reach.learn: The range the movement leaves them

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: moving every note by a fixed interval is arithmetic once pitch, duration and clef are present. She still chooses the instrument and still plays the result. The digest describes this as exact arithmetic in notation software. No digest product is cited for the shift, because the named score product turns audio into a score and this design does not record anyone.

assumptions: The composer transposes today. The actor on the shift is the composer. The machine appears only as the future interval shift.

Each source note must already have pitch, duration and clef. She produced that score, or she types a handwritten bar before the shift. A missing pitch blocks that bar. She copies the blocked bar inside the play-and-fix step, which is already counted.
Placing the corrected part in {DOCS} stays her own step. It is not a second machine save, and nobody else is invented as an approver.
The notation shift is configuration of the file she already uses. No weekly tool care is added, so upkeep is zero.
The part is for musicians in this organisation. It is not sent outside.
unknowns: How often the source is already a pitched notation file, rather than handwritten.
Whether this ensemble folder is {DOCS} or only the notation file.
research_questions: What share of transpose hours is recopying notes, against asking the musician and playing the result.

already_counted.description: She still names the instrument, plays the part and places the corrected part.

incremental.description: The interval shift uses the notation file she already keeps. No extra upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the source already has pitch and duration, the interval shift removes the recopying. When she must type a handwritten part first, most of that hour stays. She still chooses the instrument and still plays the result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Rewrite a score in another style

steps.what: Mark the rhythms, harmonies or tempos to change
Apply those rhythms, harmonies and tempos in a sketch

loop.check: Each changed bar matches a rhythm, harmony or tempo she marked, and the motif is still recognisable
loop.stop: One sketch. If a marked bar cannot be applied, that bar stays as written and she rewrites it
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed interval shift cannot apply a marked rhythm, harmony or tempo change

steps.what: Rewrite the sketch into the musical style
Play the rewrite and mark what still fails

tasks.design: She marks the rhythms, harmonies or tempos that change. A bounded draft in {OTHER} applies only those marks to her original score and leaves unmarked bars as written. She rewrites the sketch by ear. The sketch is not stored as the score.
tasks.previous_blocker: A style change is a musical judgement. A fixed transpose cannot choose swing, a new harmony or a new tempo.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she has marked the bars, a short loop can apply only those marks and stop. It cannot decide the style.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the rewrite sounds like the style she wants stays with her ear. She often discards the sketch.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses which rhythms, harmonies and tempos change, and she rewrites what the sketch gets wrong.
tasks.altitude: The first copy of bars she already marked takes less time. She still chooses the style and still rewrites by ear. The sketch is not the score.

reach.task: Ask for a second style of the same cue
reach.learn: Which style the picture can actually use

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: applying rhythm, harmony and tempo marks she already wrote can be drafted. Judging the style cannot. She rewrites the sketch. No digest product rewrites a score into another style.

The sketch is made only from her original score. Text and data mining of other works is allowed only where rightholders have not reserved it, online by machine-readable means (DSM article 4(3); Dutch Auteurswet article 15o). This design does not mine catalogues.

assumptions: The composer rewrites her own original score today. The actor on the sketch is the composer. The machine appears only as that future sketch.
Style notes list a bar and one of rhythm, harmony or tempo. She produces them. Unmarked bars are copied unchanged. Empty notes block the sketch.
The sketch is a draft she rewrites. It is not filed, and it is not sent outside.
Three hours per hundred baseline hours keep her marking examples current so the sketch does not invent changes.
The score is her musical work, not employee monitoring, so no works-council consent is assumed.
unknowns: How often her marks are specific enough that she keeps the sketch, rather than discarding it.
research_questions: What share of a style rewrite is the first copy of marked bars, against the rewrite she does by ear.

already_counted.description: She still marks the changes, rewrites by ear and plays the result.

incremental.description: Keep her marking examples current so the sketch applies only changes she named.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When her marks name exact bars, the sketch saves the first copy. When she discards the sketch, only a few hours move. She still rewrites by ear.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the music composed by others
Decide the desired effects for this ensemble
Arrange the music for those effects in rehearsal
Rehearse the arrangement and change what misses the effect

tasks.design: Nothing is generated. She reads music composed by others, chooses the effect, and arranges it with the ensemble in the room. No tool rewrites another composer's work.
tasks.previous_blocker: An arrangement is a musical judgement about someone else's piece. A template cannot hear the effect.
tasks.enabler_now: No enabler changes this task. She still arranges by ear.
tasks.still_hard: The effect, the forces and the rehearsal stay with her. Rights to arrange another composer's music are a licence question, not a drafting question.
tasks.human_edge: She decides how someone else's music should change, and she hears whether the effect lands.
tasks.altitude: Nothing in the week changes. She still arranges other people's music in rehearsal.

reach.task: Capture the arrangement in the room
reach.learn: Which forces the room can hold

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: arranging music composed by others is composition. The digest says composing stays with the person. This design does not rewrite the piece by machine.

Arranging a work composed by others touches the author's exclusive rights. Text and data mining is allowed unless rightholders reserve it, online by machine-readable means (DSM article 4(3); Dutch Auteurswet article 15o). This task does not mine or rewrite catalogues.

assumptions: The composer arranges today. No machine step is added.
A licence to arrange someone else's music, where one is required, is outside this task. She does not clear rights here.
No tool is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the piece she arranges is in the public domain or needs a licence from the rightholder.
research_questions: How often an arrangement in this company is of a work still in copyright.

already_counted.description: Reading the piece, choosing the effect, arranging and rehearsing all stay.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Arranging and rehearsal stay with her, so no hour moves.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still writes commercial music, still arranges other people's music, and still chooses style by ear. Interval transposition of a part she already stored as pitches takes less recopying. She still names the instrument, still plays the part, and still places it herself. A style sketch only copies bars she marked, and she still rewrites it.
skills_to_grow: Mark the target instrument before a part is shifted
Mark bar by bar which rhythm, harmony or tempo changes
Reject a sketch or a transposed part that does not fit the musician
role.ambitious_version: A tool that writes the jingle, arranges someone else's music, or files a part she has not played is out of scope. She still composes, arranges and listens.
